findings.text: _awaiting_pick_hold hand-builds the queued request record that reckon/crew/dispatching/requests.py:37 (_queued_request_record) owns and documents as the one place both the held path and a re-dispatch store that shape; the copy drops the due/urgency keys and the named_route/route_fallback passthrough the owner derives from dispatch_options, so an awaiting-pick request is not the same shape every other queued request has.

dispatcher_declared_difficulty re-implements the plan-path resolution that reckon/crew/picker/__init__.py:219 (_declared_difficulty) owns -- the same _resolved_plan_path call with the same resources.resolve_resource fallback and the same broad except -- instead of factoring that resolution into the owner and calling it from both sides.

The dispatcher overrides the hours _estimated_hours reports with the section's declared effort without reading its provenance, so a node carrying its own authoritative estimate (provenance 'node', as _estimated_hours at reckon/crew/routing.py:4240 returns it) reaches the pick with the section figure instead; _declared_difficulty's own docstring at reckon/crew/picker/__init__.py:232 states an estimate the node itself carries is never overridden.

route_defaulted names the literal step 'pick' for every non-timeout fallback: the only assignment to step is inside the `if error == "timeout"` branch, so a raised picker never reports the step that ran out, and the test's `assert defaulted["step"]` (tests/test_a_dispatch_waits_for_the_router.py:274) cannot fail for any value.

The third done-when case's 'it is not launched on the default lane' is asserted by calling _awaiting_pick_hold directly; the production branch at reckon/crew/dispatch_plan.py:1292-1305 that decides to call it is covered by no test, so deleting that branch leaves all four cases green and the guard is not durable at the wiring.

_dispatch_bound_seconds still reads the module constant while dispatch now honours routing.picker_timeout_seconds (reckon/crew/dispatch_picker.py:56), so a host that sets the flight key gets a within_bound telemetry flag measured against a different bound -- the drift this function's docstring promises cannot happen.

The route-defaulted marker is stored on the selection and the dispatch payload only; no obligations view lists it, so the plan's deliverable 'a route-defaulted reason that the obligations view lists' is delivered at the marker and not at the listing (the node records this under outside_scope, its fence does not include reckon/crew/obligations.py).

justifications.durability: Each added assertion names a code change that reddens it except the plan_dispatch hold, which tests/test_a_dispatch_waits_for_the_router.py:231 bypasses by calling _awaiting_pick_hold directly.
justifications.evidence: The gate at tests/test_a_dispatch_waits_for_the_router.py asserts cases 1-3 and only the marker of case 4, while the manifest records the base and head suite arms at 7 failed / 0 added with logs on disk.
justifications.fit: The module follows the surrounding style -- lazy imports inside the function and WHY-only comments -- and introduces no name the naming rules forbid.
justifications.goal_fidelity: The core of §59 lands at reckon/crew/dispatch_picker.py:693 (bound) and dispatch_plan.py:1292 (queue rather than default), but the deliverable's obligations listing is absent and route_defaulted names no real step.
justifications.reuse: Two added definitions duplicate capabilities the repository already owns -- the queued-record shape at reckon/crew/dispatching/requests.py:37 and the plan-difficulty resolution at reckon/crew/picker/__init__.py:219 -- rather than extending either owner.
justifications.scope_discipline: Every path in `git diff ed0ca92b abb19568` is one of the node's six declared write paths, and nothing the goal does not imply was edited.

verdicts.diff: Two commits (ad89560e2b, abb1956823) touching six files: the bound and its flight key, the dispatcher-side difficulty resolution, the PickRequest.estimated_hours field, the graceful skip in _declared_difficulty, the awaiting-pick hold and repick branch, the new test, and the evidence fragment.
